items.title: Mortgage and Loan Insurance Programs Under the National Housing Act-Debenture Interest Rates
items.summary: This notice announces changes in the interest rates to be paid on debentures issued with respect to a loan or mortgage insured by the Federal Housing Administration under the provisions of the National Housing Act (the Act). The interest rate for debentures issued under Section 221(g)(4) of the Act during the 6-month period beginning January 1, 2026, is 4 percent. The interest rate for debentures issued under any other provision of the Act is the rate in effect on the date that the commitment to insure the loan or mortgage was issued, or the date that the loan or mortgage was endorsed (or initially endorsed if there are two or more endorsements) for insurance, whichever rate is higher. The interest rate for debentures issued under these other provisions with respect to a loan or mortgage committed or endorsed during the 6-month period beginning January 1, 2026, is 4\3/4\ percent.

story_ideas.title: CMS refreshed dataset: Provider Information (08/01/26)
story_ideas.hook: The file holding certified bed counts, staffing figures and the quality measure scores that feed the Five-Star Rating System was republished on 08/01/26, one row per nursing home.
story_ideas.consumer: Before you tour anywhere, pull the row for each home on your shortlist and compare certified beds and staffing against the two or three others you are considering; ask the admissions director to explain any measure where their number sits below the others, and get the answer in writing.
story_ideas.b2b: Every competitor's staffing and quality inputs are current again in the same refresh, which makes this the natural moment for operators to run a market-level benchmarking pass and for referral partners to re-sort their preferred provider lists.
story_ideas.note: Localizable to US states and counties, one row per facility — supports a state-ranked table or a county-level lookup tool.

story_ideas.title: CMS refreshed dataset: Health Deficiencies (08/01/26)
story_ideas.hook: Three years of nursing home health citations, with scope and severity, correction dates and current status, went live again on 08/01/26.
story_ideas.consumer: Look up the last three years of citations for any home you are considering, check the scope and severity code rather than the raw count, and ask whether each citation has been corrected and on what date.
story_ideas.b2b: Scope-and-severity distributions by state and by ownership type are the cleanest available proxy for where survey enforcement is tightening, which matters for compliance staffing budgets and for how chains allocate regional quality directors.
story_ideas.note: Confirmed gap among monitored publishers; state and county breakouts make a heat map straightforward.

story_ideas.title: CMS refreshed dataset: Penalties (08/01/26)
story_ideas.hook: Fines and payment denials issued to nursing homes over the last three years were refreshed on 08/01/26.
story_ideas.consumer: A fine is public information, so ask the home directly about any payment denial in its record and what changed afterward; a facility that cannot describe the fix is telling you something.
story_ideas.b2b: Penalty totals cross-referenced with the Ownership file show which corporate structures are absorbing the most enforcement cost, a question that carries into underwriting, acquisition diligence and insurance renewal.
story_ideas.note: Pairs naturally with the Ownership and Health Deficiencies files for one analysis; strong Skilled Nursing News fit.

story_ideas.title: CMS refreshed dataset: Ownership (08/01/26)
story_ideas.hook: Current ownership information for every active nursing home was reissued on 08/01/26, alongside the Facility Affiliation Data refreshed 07/31/26.
story_ideas.consumer: Find out who actually owns the home you are visiting and what else that owner runs; then check whether the sister facilities carry similar deficiency and penalty records, because patterns travel across a portfolio.
story_ideas.b2b: The affiliation file lets operators and their investors map regional concentration and see which chains have grown or shed facilities since the last refresh, which is competitive intelligence rather than compliance.
story_ideas.note: Two files, two dates, one story; localizable to states and counties for a market-concentration chart.

story_ideas.title: CMS refreshed dataset: Fire Safety Deficiencies (08/01/26)
story_ideas.hook: Three years of nursing home fire safety citations, with tag numbers and correction dates, were refreshed on 08/01/26 and are entirely uncovered by monitored publishers.
story_ideas.consumer: Fire safety citations sit in a separate file from health citations, so a home with a clean health record can still have open fire safety tags; check both before you sign anything.
story_ideas.b2b: Life safety code citations are a capital expenditure signal as much as a compliance one, and the correction-date field shows how long facilities in each state are taking to close them out.
story_ideas.note: Confirmed gap; the least-reported of the inspection files and the easiest to own outright.

story_ideas.title: CMS refreshed dataset: Hospice care - State CAHPS Hospice Survey Data (08/07/26)
story_ideas.hook: State-level average scores for Medicare-certified hospice providers on the CAHPS Hospice Survey were refreshed 08/07/26, with the national file refreshed the same day.
story_ideas.consumer: Families rate hospices on things you cannot see on a tour, including communication and timeliness of help; compare your state's average against the national file before you choose, and ask a provider that trails its state average why.
story_ideas.b2b: State-versus-national CAHPS spreads identify markets where family experience scores are systematically lower, which is a recruitment and training argument for hospice operators and a referral-steering question for hospital discharge planners.
story_ideas.note: Sits in the palliative and hospice cluster, which coheres at 0.457 across CMS and RAND, with all nine items unmatched; state-level charting is built in.

story_ideas.title: BLS: Home health care services employment, August 2026 — 1,896.40 thousands of jobs (+5.0% year over year)

story_ideas.consumer: If you are trying to stay at home, the workforce is growing faster in home care than in facilities, which affects how many agencies will actually pick up your call; ask any agency how many hours it can guarantee weekly, not just whether it serves your area.
story_ideas.b2b: Wage growth of 2.0% against 5.0% headcount growth suggests agencies are expanding on volume rather than on pay, which is the number skilled nursing operators should be watching when they lose aides to home care employers.

story_ideas.title: BLS: Nursing care facilities employment, August 2026 — 1,590.20 thousands of jobs (+2.1% year over year)

story_ideas.b2b: A 2.1% growth rate sets a ceiling on census recovery, and operators should be modeling admissions against the staffing they can realistically hire rather than against licensed bed capacity.

story_ideas.title: 5 Questions and Answers About Medicaid and Provider Taxes (08/20/26)
story_ideas.hook: KFF's 08/20/26 issue brief uses its 2025-2026 survey of Medicaid directors and a proposed rule to describe how provider tax rules are changing under the 2025 reconciliation law and which states are affected.
story_ideas.consumer: Provider taxes are part of how your state pays for Medicaid long-term care, so changes here reach the nursing home and home care benefits your family may rely on; ask your state's long-term care ombudsman what is changing locally.
story_ideas.b2b: State-by-state exposure to the provider tax changes is a direct reimbursement forecast for nursing facility operators, and finance teams should be mapping it against their Medicaid census before the next rate cycle.

feature_pitch_raw:
**The pattern:** On 08/01/26 CMS reissued the entire nursing home oversight file family in one pass — Provider Information (certified beds, staffing and the quality scores behind the Five-Star system), Health Deficiencies, Fire Safety Deficiencies, Penalties, Ownership, Survey Summary, Inspection Dates, Citation Code Look-up, MDS Quality Measures, Medicare Claims Quality Measures and the Skilled Nursing Facility Quality Reporting Program file — with Facility Affiliation Data refreshed 07/31/26 and Utilization Data on 08/11/26. Inside the same window, BLS put August 2026 nursing care facilities employment at 1,590.20 thousand jobs, up 2.1% year over year, against home health care services at 1,896.40 thousand, up 5.0%. Justice in Aging published its Medicaid home and community-based services primer on 08/20/26 and the Center for Retirement Research published a comparison of long-term care in Israel and the U.S. on 09/03/26. What connects them is not the subject tag: the public record used to judge an institutional bed was rebuilt all at once, while the employment and policy evidence in the same weeks points at care delivered somewhere else. This cluster coheres, and the four sources reached the same story independently.

**Why pitch this now:** HUD published FY 2027 Fair Market Rents on 09/01/26, which take effect October 1 each year and reset what a voucher covers, and issued the Housing Trust Fund FY 2026 allocation notice on 09/04/26. KFF's 08/20/26 brief describes how provider tax rules are changing under the 2025 reconciliation law and its implementing regulations, state by state. The same facilities whose penalties, deficiencies and ownership records just went back online are heading into a fall in which their Medicaid financing rules and their residents' housing subsidies both move.

**Angle:** "The August File Drop" — a single explainer-plus-data piece for families weighing a nursing home this fall and for operators whose citation and ownership history is newly current, built on the CMS Provider Information, Health Deficiencies, Penalties and Ownership files with the BLS facility-versus-home-care employment split as the frame.

**Potential headlines:**
- Every nursing home inspection record in the country was just refreshed
- Facility jobs grew 2.1 percent last year. Home care grew 5 percent.
- What CMS quietly republished in August about the home you are considering

**Potential outlets:**
- McKnight's Long-Term Care News — Tier 1 on skilled nursing regulation and clinical operations, and the deficiency, penalty and staffing files are exactly its reporting substrate.
- Skilled Nursing News — Tier 1 on operations and finance; the ownership and facility affiliation refresh has direct business implications.
- Kiplinger — Tier 2 retirement outlet that runs long-term care costs and state comparisons, which the county- and state-level CMS files support.
- Family Caregiver Alliance — Tier 2 caregiving authority and the right distribution partner for a how-to-read-the-file guide aimed at adult children.
